en: Which tense is this sentence in? “I am reading a book.”
“am/is/are” + an -ing verb shows an action happening now: the present progressive.
Which tense is “was singing” in “She was singing when I arrived.”?
“was/were” + an -ing verb shows an action that was going on in the past: the past progressive.
Which tense is this sentence in? “We have finished our project.”
“have/has” + a past participle is the present perfect.
Which tense is this sentence in? “They played chess yesterday.”
A finished action at a time in the past uses the simple past.
Which tense is this sentence in? “He will visit us tomorrow.”
“will” + a verb talks about the future: the simple future.
Which tense is this sentence in? “The bus leaves at eight every day.”
Something that happens regularly uses the simple present.
Which tense is “had eaten” in “I had eaten before the film started.”?
“had” + a past participle is the past perfect. It shows one past action happened before another.
Which tense is this sentence in? “It was snowing all night.”
“was/were” + an -ing verb shows an action that was going on in the past: the past progressive.
Which tense is this sentence in? “She has lived here for ten years.”
“have/has” + a past participle is the present perfect.
Which tense is this sentence in? “The birds are building a nest.”
“am/is/are” + an -ing verb shows an action happening now: the present progressive.
Which word fills the gap? “Yesterday I ___ to the cinema.”
“Yesterday” tells us the action is finished and in the past, so we use the simple past “went”.
Which word fills the gap? “Look! It ___ outside.”
“Look!” shows it is happening right now, so we use the present progressive.
Which word fills the gap? “I have ___ my homework already.”
After “have” we need the past participle “done”.
Which word fills the gap? “While we ___ dinner, the phone rang.”
The eating was going on in the past when the phone rang, so we use the past progressive.
Which word fills the gap? “Tomorrow we ___ the museum.”
“Tomorrow” is in the future, so we use “will visit”.
Which word fills the gap? “She has ___ in London since 2020.”
After “has” we need the past participle “lived” to make the present perfect.
Which word fills the gap? “Every morning, Dad ___ the dog for a walk.”
A regular habit uses the simple present, and “Dad” needs “takes”.
Which word fills the gap? “Last summer we ___ in a tent.”
“Last summer” is in the past, so we use the simple past “slept”.
Which word fills the gap? “At seven o’clock last night, I ___ a bath.”
The bath was going on at a moment in the past, so we use the past progressive.
Which word fills the gap? “By the time we arrived, the film ___.”
The film started before we arrived, so we use the past perfect “had started”.
What is the simple past of “swim”?
Today I swim, yesterday I swam. “Swum” goes with “have”, as in “I have swum”.
Which sentence is in the present perfect?
Which sentence is in the past progressive?
What is the simple past of “catch”?
“Catch” is irregular: today I catch, yesterday I caught.
Which word fills the gap? “She has ___ her lunch.”
After “has” we need the past participle “eaten”.
Which sentence is in the simple future?
Which sentence is in the present progressive?
Which word fills the gap? “Have you ever ___ a camel?”
After “have” we use the past participle “seen”.
Which word fills the gap? “I ___ my keys! I can’t find them anywhere.”
The keys are lost now because of something that already happened, so we use the present perfect.
Which is the past progressive of “The dog barks”?

en.title: Verb tenses
en.teach: Tenses show when things happen: I walked (simple past), I was walking (past progressive), I have walked (present perfect), I am walking (present progressive), I will walk (simple future).
